g.text: What do the jar marks measure?
Four Harappa jars • published measurements + an additional profile reconstruction
Compare width, cross-section area and capacity against the same proposed mark counts.
Published drawing, not a photograph or generated image.
Catalogue rim sign 034; other body marks are a separate inscription.
What do the other three jars predict for this jar?
Learn one unit from those three; use this jar’s measurement to predict its count.
2 THE SAME FOUR JARS, SIDE BY SIDE
Marks below are schematic tallies of source counts, not facsimiles of the inscriptions.
3 OVERALL FIT: PREDICT EACH JAR’S COUNT FROM THE OTHER THREE
Lower error = closer predictions. Ignoring dimensions gives 44% average count error.
Area fits the four-jar panel best; width best predicts the additional jar.
The original three favor volume. Including uncertain cases can change the winner.
This does not identify an ancient unit, a language, or accounts for cloth length / land area.
Sources: Kenoyer, Fig. 7.2 (drawing); Fuls 2012, Tables 1–3 (dimensions / original capacities); released H95 inner-profile trace.
Source limits: Fuls table layout not visually verified; H95 accession/caption conflict and candidate H-2263 join retained in the source notes.
One drawing shown; four objects tested. Redrawn marks show the numerical hypothesis only. Calculations and source links accompany this chart.
